metadata.title: Théorie de la mesure dans les lieux réguliers. ou : Les intersections cachées dans le paradoxe de Banach-Tarski

nodes.name: $f^*$ and $f_*$
nodes.statement: For every continuous Function $f : X \rightarrow Y$ between topological Spaces, there exists a pair of functors $(f^*,f_*)$. \begin{gather*} f* = f^{-1} : O(Y) \rightarrow O(X)\\ f_* : O(X) \rightarrow O(Y) := A \mapsto \bigcup_{f^*(v) \le A} v\\ \end{gather*}
nodes.label: def:f_star

nodes.name: $f^* \dashv f_*$
nodes.statement: $f^*$ is the right adjoint to $f_*$
nodes.label: lem:f_star_adj

nodes.name: triangle
nodes.statement: (Mclane p. 485) The triangular identities reduce to the following equalities: \[f^*f_*f^* = f^* \quad \text{and} \quad f_*f^*f_* = f_*\]
nodes.label: lem:triangle

nodes.statement: This follows from the triangular identities of the adjunction.

nodes.name: Embedding
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemme 1) The following arguments are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $f^*$ is surjective \item $f_*$ is injective \item $f^{*}f_* = 1_{O(X)})$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:embedding

nodes.statement: This follows from the triangular identities.

nodes.name: Embedding
nodes.statement: An embedding is a morphism that satisfies the conditions of \ref{lem:embedding}
nodes.label: def:embedding

nodes.name: Nucleus
nodes.statement: A nucleus is a map $e : O(E) \rightarrow O(E)$ with the following three properties: \begin{enumerate} \item $e$ is idempotent \item $U \le e U$ \item $e(U \cap V) = e(U) \cap e(V)$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:nucleus

nodes.name: Nucleus
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemme 3) Let $e : O(E) \rightarrow O(E)$ be monotonic. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $e$ is a nucleus \item There is a locale $X$ and a morphism $f: X \rightarrow E$ such that $e = f_*f^*$. \item Then there is a locale $X$ and a embedding $f: X \rightarrow E$ such that $e = f_*f^*$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:nucleus

nodes.name: Nucleus Partial Order
nodes.statement: For two nuclei $e$ and $f$ on $O(E)$, we say that $e \le f$ if $e(U) \le f(U)$ for all $U \in O(E)$. This relation is a partial order.
nodes.label: def:nucleus_partial_order

nodes.name: Nucleus Intersection
nodes.statement: For a set $S$ of nuclei, the intersection $\bigcap S$ can be computed by $\bigcap S(a) = \bigcap \{j(a) | j \in S \}$. This function satisfies the properties of a nucleus and of an infimum. \\ Quelle: StoneSpaces S.51
nodes.label: lem:nucleus_intersection

nodes.name: Sublocal
nodes.statement: (Leroy CH 3) A sublocal $Y \subset X$ is defined by a nucleus $e_Y: O(X) \rightarrow O(X)$, such that $O(Y) = Im(e_Y) = \{U \in O(X) | e_Y(U) = U\}$. The corresponding embedding is $i_X : O(Y) \rightarrow O(X)$. $i^*_X(V) = e_X(V)$, $(i_X)_*(U) = U$ And every nucleus $e$ on $O(X)$ defines a sublocal $Y$ of $X$ by $O(Y) = Im(e)$
nodes.label: def:sublocal

nodes.name: Sublocal Inclusion
nodes.statement: (Stimmt das?)(Leroy Ch 3) $X \subset Y$ if $e_Y(u) \le e_X(u)$ for all $u$. This means that the Sublocals are a dual order to the nuclei.
nodes.label: def:sublocal_inclusion

nodes.name: factorisation
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemme 2) Let $i : X \rightarrow E$ be an embedding and $f: Y \rightarrow E$ be a morphism of spaces. To have $f$ factor through $i$, it is necessary and sufficient that $i_*i^*(V) \le f_*f^*(V) for all V \in O(E)$.
nodes.label: lem:factorisation

nodes.name: Union of Sublocals
nodes.statement: (Leroy CH 1.4) Let $(X_i)_i$ be a family of sublocals of $E$ and $(e_i)_i$ the corresponding nuclei. For all $V \in O(E)$, let $e(V)$ be the union of all $W \in O(E)$ which are contained in all $e_i(V)$.
nodes.label: def:sublocal_union

nodes.name: Union of Sublocals
nodes.statement: (Leroy CH 4) Let $X_i$ be a family of subframes of $E$ and $e_i$ be the corresponding nuclei. For every $V \in O(E)$, let $e(V)$ be the union of all $W \in O(E)$ which are contained in every $e_i(V)$. Then \\ \begin{enumerate} \item $e$ is the corresponding nucleus of a sublocale $X$ of $E$ \item a sublocale $Z$ of $E$ contains $x$ if and only if it contains all $X_i$. $X$ is thus called the union of $X_i$ denoted by $\bigcup_i X_i$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:sublocal_union

nodes.statement: The properties of the nucleus (idempotent, increasing, preserving intersection) can be verified by unfolding the definition of $e(V)$.

nodes.name: Sublocal Union equals Nucleus Intersection
nodes.statement: For a family of sublocals $X_i$ of $E$, the union $\bigcup X_i$ is the intersection of the corresponding nuclei.
nodes.label: lem:sublocal_union_nucleus_intersection

nodes.name: Intersection of Sublocals
nodes.statement: Let $(X_i)_i$ be a family of sublocal of $E$ and $(e_i)_i$ the corresponding nuclei. For all $V \in O(E)$, the intersection $\bigcap X_i$ is the Union of all Nuclei $w$ such that $w \le x_i $ for all $x_i \in X_i $
nodes.label: def:sublocal_intersection

nodes.name: Nucleus Complete Lattice
nodes.statement: The Nuclei (and therefore the sublocals) form a complete lattice.
nodes.label: lem:nucleus_complete_lattice

nodes.statement: One can prove that the Nuclei are closed under arbitrary intersections by unfolding the definition of the intersection. The supremum is defined as the infimum of the upper Bound. \\

nodes.name: Complete Heyting Algebra
nodes.statement: A complete Lattice is a Frame if and only if it as a Heyting Algebra.
nodes.label: prop:complete_heyting_algebra

nodes.statement: (Source Johnstone:) The Heyting implication is right adjoint to the infimum. This means that the infimum preserves Suprema, since it is a left adjoint.

nodes.name: Nucleus Heyting Algebra
nodes.statement: The Nuclei form a Heyting Algebra.
nodes.label: lem:nucleus_heyting_algebra

nodes.statement: Quelle Johnstone

nodes.name: Nucleus Frame
nodes.statement: The Nuclei form a frame.
nodes.label: lem:nucleus_frame

nodes.name: Direct Images
nodes.statement: Let $f : E \rightarrow F$ be a morphism of Frames. The map $f_*f^* : O(F) \to O(F)$ is the nucleus of the subframe $Im(f)$ of $F$. By (lemma 2), $Im(F)$ is the smallest subframe of $F$ through which $f$ can be factored. For any subframe $X$ of $E$, we define the direct image as \[f(x) = Im(fi_x)\] Where $i_X$ is the inclusion of $X$ into $E$.
nodes.label: def:direct_images

nodes.name: (4) Direct Images Transitive
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemme 4) Given two morphisms $f : E \rightarrow F$ and $g : F \rightarrow G$ and a subspace $X$ of $E$, we have \[(gf)(X) = g(f(X))\]
nodes.label: lem:direct_images_transitive

nodes.name: (5) Direct Images Families
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemme 5) For all morphisms $f: E \rightarrow F$ and a family $(X_i)$ of subspaces of $E$, the following holds: \[f(\cup_i X_i) = \cup_i f(X_i)\]
nodes.label: lem:direct_images_families

nodes.name: Inverse Images
nodes.statement: We have a morphism of spaces $f : E \rightarrow F$ and a subspace $Y$ of $F$. The inverse image $f^{-1}(Y)$ is the biggest subspace $X$ of $E$ such that $f(X) \subset Y$. \\ More generally for a morphism $h : A \rightarrow E$, the necessary and sufficient condition for $h$ to factor through $f^{-1}$ is that $fh$ factors through $Y$. \[Im h \subset f^{-1}(Y)\iff f(Im h) \subset Y \iff Im(fh) \subset Y \] \
nodes.label: def:inverse_images

nodes.name: $e_U$
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a space with $U, H \in O(E)$. We donote by $e_U$ the largest $W \in O(E)$ such that $W \cap U \subset H$. We verify that $e_U$ is the nucleus of a subspace, which we will temporarily denote by $[U]$.
nodes.label: def:e_U

nodes.name: $e_U$ is a nucleus
nodes.statement: The map $e_U$ is a nucleus.
nodes.label: lem:e_U_nucleus

nodes.name: Open sublocal
nodes.statement: For any $U \in O(E)$, the sublocal $[U]$ is called an open sublocal of $E$.
nodes.label: def:open_sublocal

nodes.name: (6,7) Open Sublocal Properties
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemma 6,7) \begin{enumerate} \item For all subspaces $X$ of $E$ and any $U \in O(E)$: \[X \subset [U] \iff e_X(U) = 1_E\] \item For all $U, V \in O(E)$, we have: \[[U \cap V] = [U] \cap [V]\] \[e_{U \cap V} = e_Ue_V=e_Ve_U\] \[U \subset V \iff [U] \subset [V]\] \item For all families $V_i$ of elements of $O(E)$, we have: \[\cup_i[V_i] = [\cup_iV_i]\] \item \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:sublocal_properties

nodes.name: Complement
nodes.statement: The complement of an open sublocal $U$ of $X$ is the sublocal $X \setminus U$. (Leroy p. 12)
nodes.label: def:complement

nodes.name: Complement Injective
nodes.statement: The complement is injective.
nodes.label: lem:complement_injective

nodes.name: Closed Sublocal
nodes.statement: A sublocal $X$ of $E$ is called closed if $X = E \setminus U$ for some open sublocal $U$ of $E$.
nodes.label: def:closed_sublocal

nodes.name: Intersection of Closed Sublocals
nodes.statement: For any family $X_i$ of closed sublocals of $E$, the intersection $\bigcap X_i$ is closed (it can be computed by taking the complement of the union of the complements).
nodes.label: lem:closed_intersection

nodes.name: (1.8) Properties of Complements
nodes.statement: For any open sublocal $V$ of $E$ and any sublocal $X$ of $E$, we have: \[V \cup X = E \iff E \setminus V subset X\] \[V \cap X = \emptyset \iff X \subset E \setminus V\] And thereby: \[(E - U = E - V) \implies U = V\]
nodes.label: lem:properties_of_complements

nodes.name: (1.9) Preimage of complements
nodes.statement: For any morphism of spaces $g: A \to E$ and any open sublocal $V$ of $F$, we have: \[g^{-1}(E - V) = A - g^{-1}(V)\]
nodes.label: lem:preimage_of_complements

nodes.name: (1.8bis) Properties of Complements Part 2
nodes.statement: For any open sublocal $V$ of $E$ and any sublocal $X$ of $E$, we have: \[V \cup (E - V) = E \iff V \subset X \] \[V \cap (E - V) = \emptyset X \subset V\]
nodes.label: lem:properties_of_complements_part_2

nodes.name: (1.11) Distribution of Intersections over Unions
nodes.statement: Let $X, Y, L$ be three sub locals of $E$. If $L$ is open or closed, we have: \[L \cap (X \cap Y) = (L \cap X) \cup (L \cap Y)\]
nodes.label: lem:distribution_of_intersections_over_unions

nodes.name: Further Topology
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item $Int X$ is the largest open sublocal contained in $X$ \item $Ext X$ is the largest open sublocal contained in $E \setminus X$ \item $\bar{X}$ is the smallest closed sublocal containing $X$ \item $\partial X = \bar{X} \cap (E - Int X)$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:further_topology

nodes.name: Properties of Further Topology
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item $\bar{X} = E \setminus Ext(X)$ \item $\partial X = E \setminus (Int X \cup Ext X)$ \item $Int X \cup \partial X = \bar X$ \item $Ext X \cup \partial X = E \setminus Int X$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:properties_of_further_topology

nodes.name: Induced boolean algebra
nodes.statement: Define $At(U_1,\dots,U_n)$ as the collection of all finite nonempty intersections of opens $U_i$ or their complements. \\ Define $b(U_1,\dots,U_n)$ as all unions of elements of $At(U_1,\dots,U_n)$\\ Define $b(X)$ as the union of all $b(U_1,\dots,U_n)$ for finite collections of opens $U_i$.
nodes.label: def:induced_boolean_algebra

nodes.name: (2.1) Sublocals and decompositions
nodes.statement: For any open $U$ the natural morphism $p : U \sqcup (E \setminus U)$ induces a bijection of sublocals.
nodes.label: lem:sublocals_and_decompositions

nodes.name: (2.2) Induced morphism of boolean algebras
nodes.statement: For all $H \in B(U_1,\dots,U_n)$ we have $f^{-1}(H) \in b(f^{-1}(U-1),\dots,f^{-1}(U_n))$ and \[H \mapsto f^{-1}(H) \] Is a morphism of boolean algebras
nodes.label: lem:induced_morphism_of_boolean_algebras

nodes.name: Boolean algebra
nodes.statement: (Leroy Proposition II.1) \begin{enumerate} \item $b(X)$ is the generated boolean algebra of the open and closed sublocals of $X$. \item For all $H \in b(X)$, we have $f^{-1}(H) \in b(Y)$ and the map $H \to f^{-1}(H)$ is a homomorphism of boolean algebras $b(X) \to b(Y)$ \item For two sublocals $A, B$ of $X$ and any $H \in b(X)$, we have: \[H \cap (A \cup B ) = (H \cap A) \cup (H \cap B)\] \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: prop:boolean_algebra

nodes.name: $b(X)$ generates sublocals
nodes.statement: Every sublocal $X$ is an intersection of elements of $b(X)$.
nodes.label: lem:b_X_generates_sublocals

nodes.name: Union of Intersections
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemme 2.4) For any family $B_i$ of sublocals of a local $E$ and a sublocal $A$, we have: \[A \cup (\bigcap_i B_i) = \bigcap_i (A \cap B_i)\] This implies if $A_i$ and $B_j$ are families of sublocals of $X$, we have: \[(\bigcap_i A_i)\cup(\bigcap_j B_j) = \bigcap_{ij}(A_i \cup B_j)\]
nodes.label: lem:union_of_intersections

nodes.name: Preimage commutes with unions
nodes.statement: (Leroy resultat principal) For any morphism $f$ of locals, we have: \[f^{-1}(A \cup B) = f^{-1}(A) \cup f^{-1}(B)\]
nodes.label: thm:preimage_commutes_with_unions

nodes.name: Measure on Locales
nodes.statement: A measure on a local $X$ is a map $\mu : O(X) \to [0,\infty)$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $\mu(\emptyset) = 0$ \item $U \subset V \implies \mu(U) \le \mu(V)$ \item $\mu(U \cup V) = \mu(U) + \mu(V) - \mu(V \cap V)$ \item For any increasingly filtered family $V_i$ of open sublocals of $X$, we have: \[\mu(\bigcup V_i) = \sup_i \mu(V_i)\] this means: For all $i$ and $j$ there exists a $k$ such that $V_i \cup V_j \subset V_k$ bzw. $V_i \subset V_k$ and $V_j \subset V_k$. \end{enumerate} (Leroy III.1.)
nodes.label: def:measure_on_locals

nodes.name: Caratheodory
nodes.statement: For any measure $\mu$ on a local $X$, the caratheodory extension is: \[\mu(A) = \inf \{\mu(U) | A \subset U \in O(X)\},~A\in X\]
nodes.label: def:caratheodory

nodes.name: Proptery 0 (Commutes with sup)
nodes.statement: (Leroy lemme 3.1) The caratheodory extension of a measure on a local commutes with unions of increasing families.
nodes.label: lem:commutes_with_sup

nodes.name: Caratheodory Extensions are monotonic
nodes.statement: The caratheodory extension is monotonic i.e. \[A \le B \implies \mu(A) \le \mu(B)\]
nodes.label: lem:monotonic

nodes.statement: This is a direct consequence of the definition of the caratheodory extension.

nodes.name: Subadditivity
nodes.statement: The Caratheodory extension is subaddtive: $$\mu(A \cup B) \le \mu(A) + \mu(B)$$
nodes.label: lem:caratheodory_subaddtive

nodes.name: Regular Local
nodes.statement: A local is regular, if for all open sublocals $U$ of $E$, the open sublocals $V$ such that $V\bar \subset U$ recover $U$.
nodes.label: def:regular_local

nodes.name: Neighborhood
nodes.statement: A neighborhood of a sublocal $A$ of $X$ is an open sublocal $V$ of $X$ such that $A \le V$.
nodes.label: def:neighborhood

nodes.name: Regularity of Sublocals
nodes.statement: (Leroy lemme 3.2) In a regular local, any sublocal is regular, meaning that it is the intersection of all open neighborhoods.
nodes.label: lem:regularity_of_sublocals

nodes.name: Measure add compl eq top
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemme 3.3) For any open sublocal $U$ of a local $X$, the caratheodory extension of a measure on $X$ satisfies \[\mu(U) + \mu(X \setminus U) = \mu(X)\]
nodes.label: lem:measure_add_compl_eq_top

nodes.statement: Siehe Leroy

nodes.name: Restriction
nodes.statement: The Restriction of a Measure to any open Sublocal is a Measure.
nodes.label: lem:restriction

nodes.name: Property 2
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemm 3.4) For any open sublocal $U$ and any sublocal $A$ of a local $E$, the caratheodory extension of a measure on $X$ satisfies \[\mu(A) = \mu(A \cap U) + \mu(A \cap(E\setminus U))\]
nodes.label: lem:restrict_add_compl_eq_top

nodes.statement: Siehe Leroy

nodes.name: Property 3
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemm 3.5) For a increasing family $V_{\alpha}$ of open sublocals of $E$ and any sublocal $A$, we have: \[\mu(A \cap(\bigcup V_{\alpha})) = \sup_\alpha \mu(A\cap V_\alpha)\]
nodes.label: lem:restrict_preserves_sSup

nodes.name: Restriction to a Sublocale
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a sublocale of $E$ with the embedding $i : A \rightarrow E$. The restriction of a measure $\mu$ on $E$ to $A$ is a measure on $A$: $$V \mapsto \mu(i(V)) : Open(A) \to \mathbb{R}$$
nodes.label: lem:restriction_to_sublocale

nodes.name: Elementary Properties of Caratheodory Extensions
nodes.statement: (Leroy lemme 3.3, 3.4, Corollary 3.1, Lemme 3.5) For any measure on a local $X$, the caratheodory extension satisfies the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item It is monotonic i.e. \[A \le B \implies \mu (A) \le \mu (B)\] \item Commutes with unions of increasing families \item $\mu(U) + \mu(X \setminus U) = \mu(X)$ \item $\mu(A) = \mu(A \cap U) + \mu(A \cap(E\setminus U))$ \item For a increasing family $V_{\alpha}$ of open sublocals of $E$ and any sublocal $A$, we have: \[\mu(A \cap(\bigcup V_{\alpha})) = \sup_\alpha \mu(A\cap V_\alpha)\] \item For any measure on a local $X$ and a decreasing family $V_i$ of open sublocals, the caratheodory extension fulfills: $\mu (\inf V_i) = \inf \mu(V_i)$. \end{enumerate} In particular, for two open sublocals $U$ and $V$ of $X$ and any sublocal $A$ of $X$, we have \[\mu(A \cap (U \cup V)) = \mu(A\cap U) + \mu(A\cap V) - \mu(A \cap U \cap V)\]
nodes.label: prop:elementary_properties_of_caratheodory_extensions

nodes.name: strictly additve
nodes.statement: (Leroy theorem 3.3.1) For any measure on a local $X$, the caratheodory extension is strictly additive, i.e. $\mu (A \cup B) = \mu(A) + \mu(B) - \mu(A \cap B)$.
nodes.label: prop:strictly_additive

nodes.name: reductive
nodes.statement: (Proposition 3.3.1) For any measure on a local $X$, the caratheodory extension is reductive, i.e. for all $A \le X$ the set $\{A' \subset A, \mu(A') = \mu(A)\}$ has a minimal element.
nodes.label: prop:reductive

nodes.name: Commutes with inf opens
nodes.statement: (Leroy Lemme 3.6) For any measure on a local $X$ and a decreasing family $(V_i)_{i\in I}$ of open sublocals, the caratheodory extension fulfills: $\mu (\inf_{i\in I} V_i) = \inf_{i\in I} \mu(V_i)$.
nodes.label: lem:commutes_with_inf_opens

nodes.name: Commutes with inf
nodes.statement: (Leroy lemme 3.7 et principal) For any measure on a local $X$, the caratheodory extension is regular $\mu (\inf_{i\in I} A_i) = \inf{i\in I} \mu(A_i)$. For decreasing families $(A_i)_{i\in I}$
nodes.label: prop:commutes_with_inf

nodes.name: Main Theorem (very important)
nodes.statement: For any measure on a local $X$, the caratheodory extension is \begin{enumerate} \item strictly additiv, i.e. $\mu (A \cup B) = \mu(A) + \mu(B) - \mu(A \cap B)$ for all $A,B\in X$, \item commutes with inf $\mu (\inf_{i\in\mathbb{N}} A_i) = \inf_{i\in\mathbb{N}} \mu(A_i)$ for a familiy $(A_i)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ of elements $A_i\in X$, \item reductive, i.e. for all $A \le X$ the set $\{A' \subset A, \mu(A') = \mu(A)\}$ has a minimal element. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: thm:main

nodes.name: (1.10) Intersection of Open and Closed Sublocals
nodes.statement: For any $U \in O(E)$, and sublocal $X$ of $E$ we have: \[e_{U \cap X} = e_Ue_X\] And for a closed $F$ \[e_{X \cap F} = e_Xe_F\]
nodes.label: lem:open_closed_intersection

nodes.name: Regular Top to regular local
nodes.statement: Any regular topological space induces a regular local.
nodes.label: lem:regular_top_to_regular_local

nodes.name: Opens
nodes.statement: (Leroy V.1 Remarque 2) The Open subsets of any good enough topological space correspond precisely to the open sublocals of the corresponding local.
nodes.label: lem:opens_correspond

nodes.name: Subset Sublocal
nodes.statement: (leroy V.1 Remarque 3) Any subset $X$ of a good enough topological space $E$ induces a sublocal $[X]$ of the corresponding local. This is an order preserving embedding.
nodes.label: lem:subset_sublocal

nodes.name: Good enough topological space
nodes.statement: blackbox to mathlib????
nodes.label: def:good_enough_topological_space

nodes.name: Subset to sublocal Part 1
nodes.statement: (Leroy Proposition 5.1.1) For two subspaces $X$ and $Y$ of $E$ and an open subspaces $U$ of $E$, we have: \begin{enumerate} \item $X \subset Y \implies [X] \subset [Y]$ \item $X \subset U \iff [X] \subset [U]$ \item If $E$ is a good enough topological space, then \[X \subset Y \iff [X] \subset [Y]\] \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:subset_to_sublocal_part_1

nodes.name: Subset to sublocal Part 2
nodes.statement: (Leroy Proposition 5.1.2, 5.1.3) For an open subspace $U$ of $E$ and a subspace $X$ of $E$, we have: \begin{gather*} [U \cap X] = [U] \cap [X]\\ F = E \setminus U\\ [F] = [E] \\ [U]\\ [X \cap F] = [X] \cap [F]\\ \end{gather*}
nodes.label: lem:subset_to_sublocal_part_2

nodes.name: Part 3
nodes.statement: For any subspaces $X$ of E, we have: \begin{enumerate} \item \[Ext[X] = [Ext X]\] \item \[\bar{[X]} = [\bar{X}]\] \item \[[Int X] \subset Int[X]\] \item \[\partial[X] \subset [Fr(X)]\] \end{enumerate} For a good enough topological space $E$, we have equality in 3 and 4.
nodes.label: lem:subspaces_part_3

nodes.name: Subset to sublocal preserves structure
nodes.statement: For two subspaces $X$ and $Y$ of $E$ and an open subspaces $U$ of $E$, we have: \begin{enumerate} \item $X \subset Y \implies [X] \subset [Y]$ \item $X \subset U \iff [X] \subset [U]$ \item If $E$ is a good enough topological space, then \[X \subset Y \iff [X] \subset [Y]\] \item \[[U \cap X] = [U] \cap [X]\] \item $\dots$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: prop:subset_to_sublocal_structure

nodes.name: Measure top to loc
nodes.statement: Any measure on a good enough topological space $X$ induces a measure on the corresponding local. Furthermore, the classical caratheodory extension onto $\mathcal{P}(X)$ agrees with the restriction of the caratheodory extension of the induced measure on the local.
nodes.label: thm:measure_top_to_loc
